pr_title: Fix: Fixed wrong date format when language is set to Default
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**
Items resolved / related issues by this PR.
- Closes #10692

**Details**
`ApplicationLanguages.PrimaryLanguageOverride` is empty when language is set to Windows Default, so we shuold use `ApplicationLanguages.Languages` property instead.

issue_context.title: Add locale to others languages on creation date and modified date
issue_context.body:
### What feature or improvement do you think would benefit Files?

I'm from Brazil, so as obvious another language, but when I set to my language the date shows in English.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53986027/207322844-10f3356d-4811-41da-8ea4-55793c059a01.png)



### Requirements

Just set locale based on the region's language, like windows does.

### Files Version

Versão: 2.4.0.0 OS Version: 10.0.22621.819

### Windows Version

Windows 11 22H2  22621.819

_No response_
comments:
This happens when the language setting is set to Windows Default instead of a specific language.
I will create a PR to fix this issue.

> Wasn't it discussed in #10320 already?

Yes

Closed without fix? 

On #10320 didn't resolve anything u guys told will leave as is, so the bug will keep forever?

review_comments: This doesn't seem right, does it follow the language override as well?

Yes.
https://learn.microsoft.com/uwp/api/windows.globalization.applicationlanguages.primarylanguageoverride

> When you set the PrimaryLanguageOverride, this is immediately reflected in the ApplicationLanguages.Languages property.

I have also confirmed that selecting another language instead of the default works fine.
